hooks.text: A strange orange light flickered over the East London docks.
Why did a shockwave from London reach a town in Norfolk?
Fifty tons of TNT sat just yards from crowded London homes.

title: Why Did the Silvertown Explosion Stay Secret for Decades?
description: The 1917 Silvertown explosion was London's largest blast, caused by a fire at a crowded docklands TNT factory.

beats.text: A strange orange light flickered over the East London docks.
beats.visual: Photograph of a fire at a factory in Silvertown, 1917

beats.text: At 6.52 pm, shockwaves from Silvertown reached houses in Norfolk.
beats.visual: Vintage map showing the distance between London and Norfolk
queries: map of East Anglia and London

beats.text: Neighbors feared a German air raid or secret sabotage.
beats.visual: Illustration of a Gotha G.IV German bomber over London, 1917

beats.text: Instead, 50 tons of TNT detonated in the crowded factory.
beats.visual: Photograph of the destruction caused by the Silvertown explosion, 1917

beats.text: The government report into the 73 deaths stayed secret for decades.
beats.visual: Photograph of an official government document with a TOP SECRET stamp

beats.text: It revealed officials ignored warnings because they deemed production worth the risk.
beats.visual: Photograph of a First World War era chemist in a laboratory, 1915

beats.text: Witnesses never forgot how the orange light first appeared.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Silvertown war memorial in Royal Victoria Gardens

better_than_last: Applied the 'mystery' structure by starting with a strange visual (orange light) and concluding with the hidden warnings revealed decades later.
